projects.name: HikesAlike
projects.summary: Pick a hike you enjoyed and HikesAlike lists other hikes in Europe that feel similar: comparable length, climb, highest point, landscape and typical weather. You can also describe a hike instead of naming one, and limit results to a driving time from a starting town.
details: Builds a catalogue of roughly 250,000 day hikes and day stages from OpenStreetMap, enriched with elevation, land cover and climate data.
Each hike becomes a feature vector; similarity weights are adjustable in the interface.
Optional drive-time filter through a self-hosted Valhalla routing engine.
Served as a small read-only export on Google Cloud Run.
projects.liveNote: The server sleeps when idle, so the first load can take around 20 seconds.

projects.name: Supply chain simulator
projects.summary: A small multi-echelon retail supply chain simulator. Factories, warehouses, shops and customers form a directed graph that shares one stochastic world with seasonality and disruptions. Each node runs its own replenishment policy, so ordering rules can be compared on identical random worlds.
details: Textbook inventory policies — (s,S), (s,Q), (R,S) and (R,s,S) — extended to route orders across several suppliers.
A PPO reinforcement learning policy trained against the textbook baseline with common random numbers, plus an Optuna tuner.
Optional LLM world generator and replay of real demand from the M5 (Walmart) dataset.
Work in progress on JEPA-style world-model policies on experimental branches.
A limited Streamlit demo compares four policies on one shop and includes a 30-world check of whether a gap is luck.
projects.liveNote: A limited slice of the simulator. It may take a few seconds to wake up.

projects.name: KrovLab
projects.summary: KrovLab takes a building footprint and a roof pitch and returns the geometry of a hipped roof: faces, hips, ridges, valleys and the quantities a roofer needs. When a plan cannot be roofed it returns a named failure rather than a wrong answer.
details: Weighted straight-skeleton core with no third-party dependencies.
Supports gables, knee walls, gambrels, courtyards, overhangs, several cells per project and dormers.
A Flask web demo draws the roof plan and a 3D view, accepts DXF footprints and exports OBJ and GLB meshes.
Its limitations are documented up front.
projects.liveNote: The server sleeps when idle, so the first load can take a few seconds.

projects.name: CV writer
projects.summary: A command-line tool that tailors a CV and a cover letter to one job ad, built as a LangGraph state machine of cooperating agents. Separate agents read the candidate's documents, research the company, retrieve relevant past projects, write, critique and fact-check the drafts, and turn them into PDFs. A router decides each next step, and the program pauses to ask the user whenever a decision is needed. Afterwards changes can be requested in plain English, such as adding a research stay or making the titles blue.
details: The whole program is one LangGraph state machine: 17 steps that share a single notepad of everything done so far. Separate agents handle reading the user's documents, analysing the job ad, researching the company, retrieving experience, writing, critique, fact checking and PDF generation.

A router agent asks the model what should happen next: ask the user a question, write the CV, write the cover letter, re-render a PDF, or stop. Plain Python code decides which choices the model may pick from and checks its answer, so a slip by a cheap model costs one more question, not a broken session.

Human-in-the-loop pauses: the graph saves its state and waits for the user to give the job ad, choose what to write first, supply missing details such as an e-mail address, or ask for changes, then carries on from where it stopped.
Two-stage retrieval from a portfolio file: vector similarity first, then an LLM check that each project is really relevant to the ad.

A critique loop: a critique agent scores each draft on content, ATS compatibility and job fit, and a separate fact check flags claims the user's material does not support. Refinement has a small budget of one automatic redraft, and at most one more if the draft improved. Every version is kept and the best one is chosen.
Self-repairing PDFs: an LLM writes the LaTeX, the compiler tries it, and any errors are fed back to the model for repair. Style changes can be requested after the fact without rewriting the text.

It runs from a terminal on the user's own machine with paid OpenAI and Tavily keys (a session on the sample files costs about 3 US cents), or on a local Ollama model for testing. Offline tests run without keys.
projects.liveNote: Runs locally from the command line and needs Python 3.12, LaTeX and API keys; there is no hosted demo.

projects.name: AeroGrid
projects.summary: A research demo that schedules household electricity use against real wholesale prices. It moves flexible loads, such as an EV charger, a hot-water heater, a dishwasher and a washing machine, into cheaper 15-minute slots and can charge and discharge a home battery, while the always-on base load stays as it is.
details: A receding-horizon linear program, with a small mixed-integer step for appliance cycles, solved with HiGHS through CVXPY. Energy deadlines are soft constraints, so the solver always returns a plan.

The optimiser runs inside a LangGraph loop. Replans are triggered by a new appliance start, a price surprise or a slipping EV deadline. A person stays in the loop: before moving a dishwasher or washing-machine start, the planner asks the user to accept the later, cheaper start or run the cycle now. In the recorded runs and the replay these answers are scripted, not given by a real person.
A digital twin replays real SMARD day-ahead prices for Germany and Luxembourg and runs a baseline and two optimiser strategies on the same inputs, so their costs can be compared.
It is a demo rather than production software; the known gaps are listed in the README.
projects.liveNote: An interactive replay of precomputed scenarios, not a live optimiser.
